class_function_inventory.name: _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare(self, resolver, admission_ref, streams, runtime, nonces, captures, reconstruction)
class_function_inventory.pin: two additional positional parameters versus _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare's six (captures, reconstruction) -- a deliberate, disclosed divergence (Decision point 5), not signature parity. Never calls _P4_CHECKED_RESOLVE, never calls resolver.snapshot() for its own admission read, never touches resolver._records or resolver._graph._records (that resolver has none of the former and this method must not read the latter): it is a pure reader of reconstruction's already-frozen root_pis_ref/dataset_g1_ref/dataset_g2_ref/pis/entries/expected_admission/pce_entries/cas fields. Builds common/identity/captured-port/captured-receipt/captured-set exactly as the fixed _prepare does (same signed('captured-port'/'captured-receipt'/'captured-set', ...) shape, same _P4_SIGN/_P4_BATCH_USES/_P4_SIGNER calls), with the three-field substitution table below and NO replay/evidence branch at all (subject_ref.kind is fixed to 'action' by ADR-0143 Decision point 7, so the 'if replay:' branch present in the fixed contract's own _prepare, trust.py:4979-4995, is omitted entirely -- not merely None-guarded -- for the dynamic contract).
class_function_inventory.phase0_must_pin: _prepare must explicitly refuse (not merely AttributeError-crash) if `reconstruction` is not exactly type _DynamicP4AdmissionReconstruction -- see row 3, this is the concrete defense against a caller or future refactor invoking _prepare with reconstruction still None or of the wrong shape.

Then delegates to _P4_DYNAMIC_VERIFY_BYTES exactly as the fixed contract delegates to _P4_VERIFY_BYTES.

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.summary: Matrix row 7: ADR-0144's single-derivation redesign (the correct fix for the preapproval Major about reconstruction-divergence) necessarily reduces the number of live graph-backed revocation/clock re-proofs inside one commit_p4_batch call from up to three/four (under the ORIGINAL, rejected multi-call design) to exactly one. ADR-0143 Decision point 9 (reaffirmed unmodified by ADR-0144 point 9) states the temporal admissibility gate for the dynamic authority IS 'the resolver's own fresh graph re-proof... inside commit_p4_batch's locked critical section' -- but under the now-accepted single-derivation design, that re-proof happens only ONCE, before signing, not repeated across the section. A revocation or clock advance landing after that one proof but before the batch is signed/committed is not caught by anything in this design (the 2nd/3rd checkpoints are confirmed, by direct code read, to perform only identity-pin checks, never a live revocation/clock recheck). Neither ADR-0144's Decision text nor evidence 0183's ground_truth_findings/preapproval review discusses this specific consequence of moving to single-derivation. This matrix takes no position on acceptability (the window is a single in-process critical section against a non-adversarial trusted host, per the standing authority_boundary_statement) but flags it as a genuine, concrete, demonstrable narrowing of a previously-stated safety property that the ADR text does not re-examine.

Matrix row 3 / class_function_inventory: _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare's exact defense against being called with `reconstruction=None` or a wrong-typed reconstruction is not specified by the ADR text (which only pins the happy-path ordering). This matrix recommends an explicit _hs_refuse(type(reconstruction) is _DynamicP4AdmissionReconstruction, ...) as _prepare's first line; the independent skeptic should confirm this is required for GREEN or accept the ADR's implicit reliance on commit_p4_batch's own fixed call ordering as sufficient (given commit_p4_batch is the only real caller today).

Matrix row 6: a caller holding a direct reference to authority._p4_resolver and invoking resolver.close_admission(...) outside commit_p4_batch's lock, then later making a separate authorize_capture_set call, is not discussed anywhere in ADR-0144's Decision text. This matrix's analysis (design holds, because close_admission remains stateless/side-effect-free under this ADR) follows from other stated properties but was not itself a stated design target. The independent skeptic should confirm this reasoning explicitly rather than let it pass by omission, and should flag any future change that would memoize the reconstruction onto the resolver as reopening this row.

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.summary: dskit/production/verifier.py: reconfirmed on this branch that no P4 authority/resolver/contract symbol -- fixed or dynamic, old or new (including every symbol this ADR introduces) -- is imported or re-exported by name. HistoricalStudyVerifier/HistoricalStudyCaptureDriver dispatch via isinstance(authority, CapturedAuthorizationAuthority) plus pinned-dispatch-identity checks only. No verifier.py edit is implied or required by ADR-0144. See matrix row 11 and the public_facades entry for the full grep-based confirmation.

The ADR's Closed construction profile leaves the exact extraction boundary of _dynamic_p4_reconstruct_admission_chain implicit ('extracted from _dynamic_p4_close_admission's existing body... with zero behavior change'). This matrix pins the exact boundary against the CURRENT code (class_function_inventory entry for _dynamic_p4_reconstruct_admission_chain): the helper begins at `graph_refs = tuple(resolver._graph._records)` and ends at the per-entry live-projection loop's last check, leaving the leading authority-identity/_p4_dynamic_reference_bytes/kind-role-schema checks and the trailing _p4_snapshot_integrity re-check inside _dynamic_p4_close_admission itself. The independent skeptic should confirm this exact split (rather than, e.g., a split that also extracts the trailing snapshot-integrity re-check, which would then run once instead of the twice it runs today at the start and end of _dynamic_p4_close_admission's current body).

_DynamicP4AdmissionReconstruction's exact construction idiom (namedtuple vs. frozen dataclass vs. the codebase's own hand-rolled _Frozen/_Published __slots__-plus-lock pattern) is left open by the ADR text. This matrix recommends the codebase's existing idiom for consistency (zero namedtuple/dataclass usage found anywhere else in trust.py); the independent skeptic should confirm or override this stylistic recommendation, and should independently check whether all 10 pinned fields (root_pis_ref, dataset_g1_ref, dataset_g2_ref, pis, entries, expected_admission, expected_admission_sha256, pce_entries, cas, cas_sha256) are genuinely read by some consumer, or whether one or two exist only for completeness and could be dropped as a later simplification (not a Phase 0 blocker either way).

non_goals: any edit to the fixed P4 corpus, its 500-ms clock, _FixedWormTrustedArtifactResolver, _FixedTerminalArtifactVerifier, or _p4_close_admission's v1-only grammar, all of which remain byte-identical and must continue to refuse dynamic v2/graph roots unchanged

reuse or extension of the fixed scope-intent/gate-evidence/scope-authorization/stage-admission historical-study apparatus for the dynamic domain (ADR-0143's non-goal, preserved -- this ADR reuses three existing field names required by the shared signed schema, never the pea/ces/bvp artifacts or their resolution mechanism)
any new reserve kind, signer, or key material
a second _LifecycleAuthorizationLedger class or a subclass of _SyntheticP4CapturedAuthorizationAuthority

cross-instance run-identity checks between the legacy and dynamic authorities (ADR-0143 Decision point 8 and matrix row 10's deliberate non-goal, unchanged, since this ADR does not touch _validate_capture_request)
gate: Phase 0 matrix authored by implementer; requires independent Phase 0 skeptic review before RED.
